title: Evaluating Generate–Validate–Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a baseline single‑shot LLM configuration generator against a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline (with a canary stage) on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus (2000 paired episodes) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The declared model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) and validation used a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Under the preregistered estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) the observed outcomes were: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered primary test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). The preregistered secondary descriptive summary (paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.001, 0.01]. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). We present the exact McNemar as the confirmatory outcome, explicitly label any one‑sided tests as exploratory/post‑hoc, and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit in light of sparse discordant counts, high baseline validity, validator scope, and the shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation for network operations promises reduced manual effort but raises safety risks: sequencing errors, transient invariant violations, and protected‑field interference can convert plausible command sequences into harmful actions. The community has therefore proposed architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair procedures to reduce unsafe outputs and produce auditable traces.

This study asks a tightly scoped question that isolates downstream verifier/repair effects: when baseline and guarded conditions begin from the exact same sampled initial candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics), to what degree can a deterministic validator plus a single allowed repair call (guarded pipeline with a canary) improve paired safe‑deploy outcomes relative to reusing that same initial candidate unmodified (baseline)? The shared_initial_candidate preregistration constraint ensures that any paired outcome difference can arise only from deterministic validation decisions and the permitted repair(s), not from differences in first‑pass generation (prompting, constrained decoding, or sampling variance).

Contributions. (1) A preregistered paired experiment (Npairs = 1000) with deterministic task selection from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 corpus and archived validator traces. (2) Full execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation demonstrating completed_pairs = 1000, hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005, and repair calls = 5. (3) Transparent confirmatory reporting: the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test (primary inference) did not reach two‑sided α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625); we archive and interpret the preregistered descriptive bootstrap summaries and label any directional one‑sided tests as exploratory.
sections.related_work:
Large surveys and controlled studies document LLM hallucination, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures that degrade correctness for code and configuration tasks [1],[2]. Research in constrained decoding and schema‑aware planning reports reductions in syntactic and executable errors in several structured domains, although many demonstrations come from non‑NetOps domains and therefore depend on validator/tool fidelity when transferred to networking tasks [3].

Recent NetOps and agentic‑AI systems work emphasizes verifier‑assisted repair, guarded execution pipelines, and governance/proof‑carrying proposals as architectural mitigations; these works present prototypes and benchmark evidence that validate verifier‑assisted designs in constrained settings while also noting that operational reliability depends on validator coverage and externally enforced protocols rather than on any single model alone [4],[5],[6].

Our experiment complements this literature by preregistering a paired estimand that isolates the incremental effect of deterministic downstream validation and a single, bounded repair call given an identical initial generation. This prevents conflation of downstream interventions with first‑pass generation changes and clarifies the limited causal claim supported by the run.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design fidelity. The study preregistration (cand‑003‑stud‑001) was finalized and frozen before any hosted‑model invocation. The confirmatory design is paired binary with task_count = 1000 deterministic tasks (challenging_workflow_stress_v1), generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1, primary_estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, and primary_test = exact two‑sided McNemar. The preregistration includes a preregistered descriptive secondary summary: paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). The preregistration and execution manifests are archived with the run.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and interpretive consequences. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused for both arms; the guarded arm could accept the candidate, reject it via deterministic validation, and—if rejected—invoke at most one permitted repair call. Therefore, any paired outcome differences are attributable only to validator decisions and the permitted repair(s). This design does not test independent first‑pass generation variants (for example, alternative prompts, constrained decoding arms, or independent sampling) because those arms were not executed under the frozen preregistration.

Models, validator, and runtime caveat. The declared model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) and the adapter family was hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Validation used a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) that enforces workflow policies: required command presence and ordering, protected‑field noninterference, and other manifest constraints to produce a deterministic safe‑deploy verdict per episode. The recorded execution/model_configuration.json lists temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0.

Task corpus, selection rule, and scoring. Tasks are synthetic intent→configuration problems containing initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty labels (very_hard, extreme). Task selection used a deterministic ordinal mapping from the preregistered challenging_workflow_stress_v1 profile to produce exactly 1000 unique tasks; seeds and selection rules were fixed prior to model calls. Scoring used scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation returning a binary validity outcome required for the paired analysis. The validator archives structured traces (validation_before/after, parsed command counts, violation codes) per episode.

Execution controls and missingness. The preregistered retry policy limited model attempts (maximum_attempts_per_call = 1) and specified missingness treatments (primary = complete_pair_primary; sensitivity = failure_as_zero). The executor recorded completed_episode_count = 2000 and failed_episode_count = 0; the analysis adhered to the preregistered treatment rules.
sections.results:
Execution and deterministic reconciliation. The run executed on 2026‑09‑01 and completed all planned episodes: planned_episode_count = 2000; completed_episode_count = 2000; complete_pairs = 1000; failed episodes = 0. Provider audit shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005 with stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation = 1000, repair = 5}; cross‑condition cache reuse was not observed. Contamination checks found no prompt‑leakage flags and the contamination_summary is empty; missingness_summary records zero failed or unscorable episodes. All deterministic consistency checks passed and artifact hashes for condition_summary.csv and paired_contingency_table.csv are archived.

Primary paired outcomes. The preregistered contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered primary confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) returns p = 0.0625 and therefore does not meet the preregistered two‑sided α = 0.05 threshold; preregistered H1 (two‑sided) is not supported.

Bootstrap and exploratory summaries. The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) yields [0.001, 0.01]. This descriptive interval excludes zero because bootstrap resampling behavior with extremely sparse discordant counts (here n10 + n01 = 5) can produce nonzero percentile bounds; the bootstrap summary was preregistered as descriptive only. A one‑sided McNemar test (guarded > baseline) yields p = 0.03125; because a directional one‑sided McNemar was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration it is reported explicitly as exploratory/post‑hoc and does not alter the preregistered confirmatory conclusion.

Repair mechanics and representative traces. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred. Representative episode artifacts show the validator rejecting an initial candidate for required_sequence violations or protected_interface touches, the adapter issuing the single allowed repair call, and the validator accepting the repaired candidate after revalidation. All raw responses, provider call traces, repair traces (where present), and validator traces are archived and referenced in the execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation artifacts. Total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5).
sections.discussion:
Inferential primacy and why results appear mixed. The preregistered primary inference is the exact two‑sided McNemar test (p = 0.0625); because that test fails to reject at α = 0.05 we report the confirmatory outcome as a non‑significant paired improvement. The paired bootstrap CI ([0.001, 0.01]) is a preregistered descriptive metric that can exclude zero under sparse discordant counts; it therefore does not override the preregistered confirmatory result. Any directional one‑sided statistics are explicitly labeled exploratory/post‑hoc.

Power assumptions and practical interpretation. The preregistered power plan assumed baseline ≈ 0.60 and targeted an absolute 0.15 increase for >80% power. Observed baseline = 0.995 is far higher than that assumption; near‑unity baseline rates produce very few discordant pairs and sharply reduce sensitivity of paired tests. Thus the design had limited power to detect small absolute gains in this observed regime. This mismatch—recorded in the preregistration and manifest—explains why a small empirical guarded improvement (0.005) does not produce two‑sided significance despite a bootstrap interval that excludes zero.

Mechanistic implications within shared_initial_candidate semantics. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics only downstream validation and permitted repair(s) can create paired differences. The five repairs illustrate that a deterministic validator with suitable rule coverage can correct specific ordering/sequence violations. However, the low repair invocation count constrains inference: it may reflect (a) few initial violations in this synthetic corpus, (b) generator behavior for the chosen model and prompt producing largely valid candidates, or (c) validator coverage that does not capture other semantic error classes. Distinguishing among these requires preregistered follow‑ups that vary generator semantics, repair budget, and validator rule sets.

Threats to validity and external generalizability. Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary is defined relative to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 rule coverage; omitted policy checks would inflate measured success. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics correctly isolate downstream effects but preclude measuring generation/prompting interventions. External validity: the synthetic corpus and single‑model scope (gpt‑5‑mini) limit generalization to heterogeneous, multi‑vendor production environments. Conclusion validity: the very small number of discordant pairs reduces the robustness of exact paired tests and increases sensitivity to discrete sampling effects.

Operational implications and preregistered follow‑ups. Artifact‑grounded evidence shows verifier‑guided repair can avert some unsafe outcomes in synthetic workflows, but measurable marginal gains depend on baseline failure prevalence, validator sensitivity/coverage, and repair budget. Preregistered follow‑ups supported by the archive: (1) run an independent first‑pass generation arm (no shared_initial_candidate) to measure prompt/decoding intervention effects; (2) sweep repair budgets (0..k repairs) to quantify marginal returns per failure class; (3) broaden validator rule suites and topology heterogeneity to probe external validity; (4) evaluate multiple model families to map model dependence. Each follow‑up should realign power calculations to plausible baseline failure rates and preregister analysis choices.
sections.conclusion: In this preregistered paired study with shared_initial_candidate semantics on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total model calls used = 1005. The confirmatory result is the preregistered McNemar outcome; directional one‑sided statistics are exploratory because they were not prespecified. These artifact‑grounded results indicate that downstream validator/repair safeguards can prevent some unsafe outcomes in synthetic scenarios, but measurable marginal gains are limited when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when the paired design intentionally isolates downstream effects. All preregistration, execution manifests, raw outputs, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived to enable reproducibility and to inform preregistered follow‑ups that broaden model diversity, validator coverage, and repair budgets.

disclosure_statement: Declared model/provider: gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). Orchestration and validator: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (digital‑twin validator). Preregistration: cand‑003‑stud‑001 (frozen prior to any hosted‑model calls). Research‑director pre‑lock constraint: topic family limited to “Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps.” Immutable initial master prompt reference archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). After the autonomy lock, literature review, preregistration finalization, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and automated revisions were performed by the autonomous research run; no human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains. This mismatch is reported explicitly and reduces the study's ability to detect very small practical effects using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
